description: Verify that DUT responds to a basic ICMP Echo Request with an Echo Reply — the canonical 'ping reply' check (RFC 792 MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
The most basic ICMP behaviour: respond to ping. This case is the positive control for the family of TYPE_05/08/09/10/11/12 cases that validate specific aspects of the Echo exchange. If this fails, none of those finer checks are meaningful.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ICMP Echo Request (type=8) with target_ip = DUT IP

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ICMP Echo Reply (type=0)

[Pass condition]
DUT emits an Echo Reply within the window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_timeout — DUT did not respond. Indicates ICMP receive path is broken or ping is disabled.

verdicts.Fail_timeout: DUT did not reply to ping — receive path broken or filtered
